pages.title: High extraversion: creating momentum while leaving room for other voices
pages.summary: A high extraversion result suggests frequent social approach, visible initiative, or energetic engagement; it does not measure confidence, social skill, happiness, popularity, or leadership ability.
pages.meaning: This range points to a relatively strong tendency to approach interaction, express a position, or activate quickly around people and events. Sociability, assertiveness, and energy level can differ, so a broad result does not require enjoying every gathering, speaking first in every meeting, or maintaining constant physical activity.
pages.possible_patterns: You may start conversations, make an implicit question discussable, convene people around an idea, or think more clearly through live exchange. The same momentum can become costly when rapid responses crowd out reflection, a full calendar exceeds recovery capacity, or visible enthusiasm is mistaken for shared agreement.
pages.counterexample: Someone in this range can need solitude after an intense day, dislike networking events, listen carefully, or stay quiet when the topic is unfamiliar. High extraversion concerns recurring approach and activation patterns, not nonstop talking, fearlessness, or dependence on an audience.
pages.context_variation: Expression may increase with familiar people, clear roles, meaningful topics, and permission to improvise. Conflict, status differences, unfamiliar language, sensory overload, exclusion, fatigue, or a setting that punishes interruption can reduce visible participation without establishing a different underlying range.
pages.combination_effects: With higher conscientiousness, social initiative may be converted into scheduled coordination and explicit follow-up; with lower conscientiousness, activity may generate more starts than closure. Higher agreeableness can make assertiveness warm and inclusive, while lower agreeableness may make disagreement more direct or competitive.
pages.strengths_tradeoffs: Potential strengths include mobilizing a group, surfacing information quickly, and sustaining energy through shared work. Tradeoffs can include taking disproportionate airtime, overbooking interaction, deciding before quieter evidence arrives, or assuming others want the same stimulation level. None of these outcomes is automatic.
pages.communication_action: In the next group discussion, state your view once, ask a specific open question, and wait through a full pause before adding more. Afterward, compare your intended contribution with actual airtime and energy cost, then protect one recovery block before accepting another optional interaction.
pages.not_meaning: This result does not mean more confident, socially skilled, likable, cheerful, persuasive, courageous, or suited to every public-facing role. It is not a diagnosis, hiring rule, leadership score, relationship forecast, or guarantee of influence and belonging.
pages.method_boundary: A range label compresses a continuous self-report result and can hide facet differences, cultural display rules, accessibility, current energy, and the safety of a setting. Interpret repeated choices and meaningful exceptions; group research cannot certify one person's result or turn it into a fixed social identity.

visible_sources.citation_label: Soto & John (2017), BFI-2 domains and facets
visible_sources.limitation: Supports a named hierarchical trait model, not the accuracy of an individual FermatMind range result.

visible_sources.citation_label: Roberts, Walton, & Viechtbauer (2006), personality trait change
visible_sources.limitation: Reports group-level patterns across studies; it does not predict how or whether one person's result will change.

pages.title: 外向性较高：推动互动，也为其他声音留下空间
pages.summary: 外向性较高表示你较常主动接近互动、公开表达立场或迅速进入活跃状态，但不代表自信、社交技能、快乐、受欢迎程度或领导能力。
pages.meaning: 这个区间提示你较常靠近人群与事件，主动表达观点，或在交流中迅速提高行动能量。社交性、自信表达和活力三个侧面可能并不整齐，所以总分较高不要求你喜欢每场聚会、每次会议都先发言或一直保持高活动量。
pages.possible_patterns: 你可能主动开启对话、把隐含问题带到桌面、召集成员推进想法，或通过现场交换更快理清思路。代价可能出现在快速回应挤掉反思时间、密集日程超过恢复容量，或把自己明显的热情误当成所有人的共识。
pages.counterexample: 外向性较高的人也可能在高强度一天后需要独处、不喜欢陌生社交、耐心倾听，或在不熟悉主题上保持安静。这个结果描述重复出现的接近与激活模式，不是永远说话、毫无畏惧或必须依赖观众。
pages.context_variation: 面对熟悉的人、清楚角色、真正关心的主题和允许临场发挥的环境时，表达通常更明显；冲突、地位差异、陌生语言、感官过载、被排斥、疲劳或惩罚插话的规则都可能让参与下降。
pages.combination_effects: 与较高尽责性组合时，社交主动更可能转成明确排期、协调与跟进；与较低尽责性组合时，活动可能带来更多起点而非收尾。较高宜人性会让表达更温和包容，较低宜人性则可能让分歧更直接或更有竞争感。
pages.strengths_tradeoffs: 潜在优势是快速动员团队、让信息浮现，并通过共同工作维持能量；潜在代价是占用过多发言时间、安排过密互动、在安静证据出现前就做决定，或假定别人需要同样的刺激水平。这些都不是分数自动造成的结果。
pages.communication_action: 下一次小组讨论只完整陈述一次观点，再提出一个具体开放问题，并等过一个完整停顿后才补充。会后比较原本想贡献的内容、实际发言空间和能量成本，并在接受下一项可选互动前保留恢复时段。
pages.not_meaning: 它不代表更自信、更会社交、更讨人喜欢、更快乐、更有说服力、更勇敢，也不代表适合所有公开岗位。它不是医疗诊断、招聘规则、领导力分数、关系预测或影响力保证。
pages.method_boundary: 区间标签压缩了连续自评结果，也可能遮住侧面差异、文化表达规则、无障碍条件、当前能量与场景安全感。解释时要同时寻找重复选择和重要反例，不能用群体研究证明个人结果准确或固定社交身份。

visible_sources.citation_label: Soto 与 John（2017）：BFI-2 维度与侧面
visible_sources.limitation: 支持一个明确命名的层级特质模型，不证明个人费马测试区间结果准确。

visible_sources.citation_label: Roberts、Walton 与 Viechtbauer（2006）：人格特质变化
visible_sources.limitation: 报告跨研究的群体变化模式，不能预测某个个人是否或如何变化。

pages.title: Middle extraversion: adjusting participation to purpose and stimulation
pages.summary: A middle extraversion result is a selective engagement pattern, not a lack of personality: approach, assertiveness, and activation may rise with purpose, familiarity, or role and recede elsewhere.
pages.meaning: This range suggests that outward engagement and lower-stimulation participation are both available strategies. The threshold may change with topic, group size, familiarity, role clarity, energy, and whether live exchange adds value. It can also reflect mixed facets rather than three scores sitting uniformly near the center.
pages.possible_patterns: You may lead discussion when you own the decision but observe when expertise lies elsewhere, enjoy a purposeful small group while declining an unstructured event, or seek company after solitary work and quiet after a dense meeting. The pattern is conditional rather than featureless.
pages.counterexample: One lively presentation does not establish a high range, and one quiet evening does not establish a low range. Someone here can speak forcefully when the stakes are clear or choose an asynchronous channel when immediate discussion would add noise rather than understanding.
pages.context_variation: Trusted relationships, a defined contribution, moderate stimulation, and time to prepare may increase participation. Large unfamiliar groups, unclear turn-taking, repetitive small talk, fatigue, or a need for uninterrupted concentration may reduce it. The useful question is which conditions move the engagement threshold.
pages.combination_effects: Higher openness may make participation rise around novel ideas while routine social contact remains limited; lower openness may favor familiar groups and established roles. Higher neuroticism can raise the threshold in evaluative settings, whereas lower neuroticism may make spontaneous contribution easier.
pages.strengths_tradeoffs: Potential strengths include moving between visible and listening roles, matching interaction to purpose, and translating across different stimulation preferences. Tradeoffs can include appearing inconsistent, failing to state participation needs, or waiting for a perfect role before contributing when a small intervention would help.
pages.communication_action: Before the next group task, choose your intended mode: lead, contribute, listen, or follow up asynchronously. State that mode and one condition that would change it. Afterward, review whether participation matched the task's purpose and your recovery cost rather than an assumed social standard.
pages.not_meaning: Middle does not mean bland, indecisive, half-introverted, universally adaptable, equally energetic everywhere, or average in social ability. It does not guarantee balance and must not be converted into a diagnosis, fixed type, hiring judgment, or relationship forecast.
pages.method_boundary: A cut label cannot show the exact score, uncertainty, facet profile, cultural norms, or stimulation conditions behind a response. Use it to investigate participation thresholds across comparable settings, not to claim a universal midpoint or explain one social success or withdrawal by trait alone.

visible_sources.citation_label: Soto & John (2017), BFI-2 domains and facets
visible_sources.limitation: Supports hierarchical trait measurement, not a universal meaning for every middle-range score.

visible_sources.citation_label: Roberts, Walton, & Viechtbauer (2006), personality trait change
visible_sources.limitation: Group-level change evidence does not establish individual score movement or explain one context shift.

pages.title: 外向性中间区间：根据目的与刺激强度调整参与方式
pages.summary: 中间区间具有明确的选择性参与模式：接近互动、公开表达和激活程度会随目的、熟悉度与角色上升，也会在其他场景主动降低。
pages.meaning: 这个区间说明外显参与与低刺激参与都可能成为你的可用策略，选择哪一个会受主题、人数、熟悉度、角色清晰度、当前能量和现场交换是否真正有价值影响。它也可能来自三个侧面强弱不同，而不是每项都正好居中。
pages.possible_patterns: 当你负责决策时可能主动带讨论，专业判断在别人手中时则先观察；你也可能喜欢目标清楚的小组，却拒绝没有结构的大型活动，或在独自工作后找人交流、密集会议后转向安静。
pages.counterexample: 一次活跃展示不能证明外向性很高，一个安静夜晚也不能证明外向性很低。中间区间的人可以在后果清楚时强势表达，也可以在即时讨论只会增加噪音时改用异步渠道。
pages.context_variation: 可信关系、明确贡献、适中刺激和准备时间可能提高参与；大型陌生群体、轮次规则不清、重复寒暄、疲劳或需要长时间专注时，参与会下降。更值得观察的是哪些条件推动参与门槛移动。
pages.combination_effects: 较高开放性可能让你在新观念周围变得活跃，即使日常社交有限；较低开放性可能更偏好熟悉群体和既定角色。较高神经质会在被评价场景提高表达门槛，较低神经质则可能让临场参与更容易。
pages.strengths_tradeoffs: 潜在优势是在带领与倾听角色之间移动、让互动匹配真实目的，并理解不同刺激偏好；潜在代价是看起来前后不一、没有说明参与需求，或等到角色完全合适才行动，错过一个小贡献就能改善协作的时点。
pages.communication_action: 下一次小组任务前，先选定带领、贡献、倾听或异步跟进中的一种模式，并说明什么条件会让你切换。结束后复盘参与是否匹配任务目的与恢复成本，而不是匹配想象中的社交标准。
pages.not_meaning: 中间区间不代表性格平淡、优柔寡断、一半内向、处处适应、所有环境能量相同或社交能力普通。它不自动保证平衡，也不能被换算成医疗诊断、固定类型、招聘判断或关系预测。
pages.method_boundary: 区间切分无法显示精确分数、不确定性、侧面组合、文化规则和刺激条件。它适合帮助你调查可比较场景中的参与门槛，不适合宣称所有环境都稳定居中，也不能单靠特质解释一次社交成败或退出。

visible_sources.citation_label: Soto 与 John（2017）：BFI-2 维度与侧面
visible_sources.limitation: 支持层级特质测量，不代表所有中间区间分数都有同一种含义。

visible_sources.citation_label: Roberts、Walton 与 Viechtbauer（2006）：人格特质变化
visible_sources.limitation: 群体变化证据不能证明个人分数移动，也不能解释一次情境差异。

pages.title: Low extraversion: contributing with lower stimulation and deliberate visibility
pages.summary: A low extraversion result suggests less frequent social approach, outward assertiveness, or high activation; it does not mean shy, anxious, unfriendly, passive, unconfident, or unable to lead.
pages.meaning: This range points to a relatively stronger preference for lower-stimulation settings, selective interaction, or time to form a response before making it public. Facets can diverge: someone may enjoy company but rarely take the floor, speak assertively when prepared but need substantial recovery, or maintain steady energy without seeking frequent social contact.
pages.possible_patterns: You may prefer written thought before a meeting, deepen one-to-one conversations, wait until a contribution is formed, or protect long blocks of solitary focus. Risks can appear when silence is read as agreement, useful knowledge arrives after the decision, invitations depend on visible enthusiasm, or recovery needs remain unspoken.
pages.counterexample: A person in this range can deliver a compelling presentation, manage a team, enjoy a celebration, confront a problem directly, or form close relationships. Lower extraversion is not evidence of fear, poor communication, low warmth, weak ambition, or an inability to act publicly.
pages.context_variation: Preparation, clear turn-taking, smaller groups, meaningful topics, asynchronous options, and predictable recovery can increase contribution. Repeated interruptions, noisy environments, forced immediacy, unfamiliar groups, or dense social scheduling can reduce visibility without reducing insight or concern.
pages.combination_effects: With higher conscientiousness, lower-stimulation work may still include reliable updates and prepared interventions; with lower conscientiousness, private intentions may need more external cues to become visible. Higher agreeableness can support attentive listening, while lower agreeableness may enable concise dissent even with little social approach.
pages.strengths_tradeoffs: Potential strengths include sustained independent focus, careful listening, and contributing after information has been processed. Tradeoffs can include delayed influence, under-signaled interest, fewer informal connections, or others filling silence with inaccurate assumptions. Value depends on the task and communication design.
pages.communication_action: Before one important discussion, write your main point and send or state it within the first third of the decision window. Request a clear turn or asynchronous follow-up if needed, then schedule recovery after the interaction. Do not require yourself to perform constant enthusiasm to prove commitment.
pages.not_meaning: This result does not mean shy, socially anxious, cold, passive, inarticulate, unmotivated, lonely, or incapable of leadership and connection. It is not a diagnosis, deficit label, hiring exclusion, relationship prediction, or instruction to avoid social growth.
pages.method_boundary: Self-report ranges can reflect current energy, role expectations, communication access, culture, and environmental stimulation as well as recurring tendencies. Compare similar settings and test participation supports; do not infer a clinical cause or fixed capacity from a group-level trait label.

visible_sources.citation_label: Soto & John (2017), BFI-2 domains and facets
visible_sources.limitation: Supports a named domain-and-facet structure, not a diagnosis or forecast for one individual's social functioning.

visible_sources.citation_label: Roberts, Walton, & Viechtbauer (2006), personality trait change
visible_sources.limitation: Aggregated change estimates do not prescribe an intervention or guarantee individual change.

pages.title: 外向性较低：用较低刺激和有意可见的方式参与
pages.summary: 外向性较低表示你较少主动接近社交、公开占据表达位置或维持高激活，但不代表害羞、焦虑、不友好、被动、不自信或无法带领。
pages.meaning: 这个区间提示你可能更偏好较低刺激、选择性互动，或在公开表达前留出形成回应的时间。三个侧面仍可能分开：有人喜欢陪伴却很少抢发言，也有人准备后能坚定表达，但高强度互动后需要较多恢复。
pages.possible_patterns: 你可能先写后说、深入一对一交流、等观点成形再贡献，或保护长段独立专注。风险可能出现在沉默被误解为同意、有用信息在决定后才出现、机会依赖可见热情，或恢复需求从未对协作者说明。
pages.counterexample: 外向性较低的人仍可完成有感染力的展示、管理团队、享受庆祝活动、直接面对问题并建立亲密关系。较低结果不能证明恐惧、沟通差、缺少温度、没有抱负或无法公开行动。
pages.context_variation: 准备时间、清楚轮次、小型群体、有意义主题、异步选择和可预期恢复会提高贡献；持续打断、噪声、强迫即时回应、陌生群体或密集社交日程则会降低可见度，但不等于洞察或关心减少。
pages.combination_effects: 与较高尽责性组合时，低刺激工作仍可能包含可靠更新和准备充分的介入；与较低尽责性组合时，私人意图可能需要外部线索才能被看见。较高宜人性支持专注倾听，较低宜人性则可能让简洁异议更容易表达。
pages.strengths_tradeoffs: 潜在优势是持续独立专注、认真倾听，并在处理信息后贡献；潜在代价是影响出现较晚、兴趣信号不足、非正式连接较少，或他人用错误假设填补沉默。哪一面重要取决于任务与沟通设计。
pages.communication_action: 面对一次重要讨论，先写下主要观点，并在决策窗口前三分之一内发出或说出；需要时主动请求明确轮次或异步跟进，再为互动后安排恢复。不要要求自己持续表演热情来证明投入。
pages.not_meaning: 它不代表害羞、社交焦虑、冷漠、被动、不善表达、没有动力、孤独或无法领导与连接。它不是医疗诊断、缺陷标签、招聘排除、关系预测，也不是拒绝社交成长的指令。
pages.method_boundary: 自评区间会同时受到当前能量、角色期待、沟通可达性、文化与环境刺激影响。要比较相似场景并测试参与支架，不能用群体特质标签推断临床原因或固定个人能力。

visible_sources.citation_label: Soto 与 John（2017）：BFI-2 维度与侧面
visible_sources.limitation: 支持明确命名的维度与侧面结构，不支持对个人社交功能做诊断或预测。

visible_sources.citation_label: Roberts、Walton 与 Viechtbauer（2006）：人格特质变化
visible_sources.limitation: 汇总变化估计不能规定个人干预，也不能保证某个人发生改变。

pages.title: High extraversion interaction audit: budget social energy and shared airtime
pages.summary: This legacy page is an interaction-budget protocol for people who create momentum through contact: map optional and essential exchanges, protect recovery, and redistribute speaking space.
pages.meaning: Use this page when social initiative is useful but the interaction load or speaking pattern has become difficult to evaluate. The task is not to suppress energy. It is to distinguish contact that advances connection or decisions from activity that consumes recovery and leaves less room for other contributions.
pages.possible_patterns: The calendar may fill with optional calls, live discussion may replace work that needs concentration, or your response speed may set an unintended pace for everyone. In groups, adding examples after the point is understood can crowd out slower processors even when the intention is enthusiasm rather than control.
pages.counterexample: Frequent interaction is not excessive when the work genuinely requires coordination, and speaking at length is not automatically unfair when you hold essential context. The audit asks whether purpose, alternatives, consent, and airtime are explicit rather than treating visible energy as a problem.
pages.context_variation: Load can rise in launch periods, community roles, shared offices, or teams that default every question to a meeting. It may become sustainable when decisions have owners, asynchronous channels are credible, invitations state whether attendance is optional, and recovery is scheduled before the calendar is full.
pages.combination_effects: Higher agreeableness may encourage inclusive invitations but make it harder to end low-value contact; lower agreeableness may support sharper limits while requiring care in tone. Higher conscientiousness can preserve follow-up, yet it may also turn every informal exchange into another tracked obligation.
pages.strengths_tradeoffs: An interaction budget can preserve connection, rapid coordination, and visible encouragement while reducing stimulation debt. The tradeoff is tolerating pauses, letting some questions remain asynchronous, and accepting that a group may reach a strong result without matching your preferred pace or energy.
pages.communication_action: List recurring interactions by purpose, required participants, best channel, and recovery cost. Convert one optional meeting to asynchronous input, add a pause after your first contribution, and invite someone who has not spoken. Protect a recovery block before adding the next nonessential event.
pages.not_meaning: This audit does not label enthusiasm as selfish, require silence, prove poor listening, or recommend withdrawing from meaningful relationships. The associated range is not a diagnosis, popularity score, leadership credential, or guarantee that other people experience the interaction positively.
pages.method_boundary: The protocol is an editorial reflection tool, not a validated treatment or an individualized measure of airtime fairness. Team power, role demands, accessibility, culture, and communication design can dominate behavior; use observed patterns and feedback rather than assigning cause to personality alone.

visible_sources.citation_label: Soto & John (2017), BFI-2 domains and facets
visible_sources.limitation: Provides domain-and-facet terminology, not validation of this interaction-budget protocol.

visible_sources.citation_label: Roberts, Walton, & Viechtbauer (2006), personality trait change
visible_sources.limitation: Group-level change research does not show that this audit will change an individual's trait or interaction pattern.

pages.title: Low extraversion participation plan: make contribution visible without constant performance
pages.summary: This legacy page is a quiet-participation protocol: identify the decision window, prepare one contribution, choose an accessible channel, request a turn, and protect recovery.
pages.meaning: Use this page when useful knowledge or interest stays private because the environment rewards immediate, repeated visibility. The objective is not to imitate a highly expressive style. It is to make one relevant contribution observable at the right time while preserving a sustainable stimulation level.
pages.possible_patterns: A decision may close before your view is fully formed, a fast group may treat silence as consent, or opportunities may go to people who signal interest publicly. Waiting for complete wording can then reduce influence, while forcing continuous participation can consume the energy needed for the substantive work.
pages.counterexample: Silence is sometimes the right contribution when no new information is available, and choosing not to attend an optional event is not avoidance by definition. The plan applies only when you want to affect a decision, relationship, or opportunity and the current channel hides that intent.
pages.context_variation: The useful support may be a pre-read, an agenda question, a named speaking turn, a written follow-up, or a smaller conversation. In a psychologically unsafe or inaccessible setting, individual preparation may not solve the structural problem; changing the channel or involving an ally may matter more.
pages.combination_effects: Higher conscientiousness can support preparation but may delay sharing until the contribution feels polished; lower conscientiousness may benefit from a short external deadline. Higher openness can make written exploration rich, while a clear decision question is still needed to convert it into timely influence.
pages.strengths_tradeoffs: A quiet-participation plan protects depth, listening, and recovery while reducing the chance that others misread absence of display. Its tradeoff is that intentional visibility still uses energy, some conversations remain fast, and one prepared point cannot control how a group receives it.
pages.communication_action: Choose one upcoming decision and write a two-sentence contribution before it starts. Send it in advance or request a specific turn, name any follow-up you will provide, and schedule recovery afterward. If the channel still excludes the contribution, record that design issue instead of blaming the range result.
pages.not_meaning: This plan does not prove shyness, require more sociability, promise influence, replace psychological safety, or imply that every silence should be corrected. A lower range is not a diagnosis, fixed deficit, hiring exclusion, relationship barrier, or reason to ignore access needs.
pages.method_boundary: This participation sequence is a practical editorial tool, not a clinically validated intervention or evidence that one trait caused low visibility. Power, language, disability, culture, role clarity, and group facilitation may be decisive; keep the range as one hypothesis among several.

visible_sources.citation_label: Soto & John (2017), BFI-2 domains and facets
visible_sources.limitation: Provides trait terminology, not proof that a score caused low visibility or that this plan is effective.

visible_sources.citation_label: Roberts, Walton, & Viechtbauer (2006), personality trait change
visible_sources.limitation: Aggregated personality change findings do not validate this participation sequence for an individual.
